headline: Apple takes OpenAI to court over stolen secrets

sources.title: Apple sues OpenAI alleging trade secret theft
Apple accuses OpenAI of using stolen trade secrets in new lawsuit
Apple sues OpenAI, alleging the AI company stole trade secrets

chunks.text: Two of the biggest names in technology have {{fallen out}}. Apple, the company behind the iPhone, has filed a [[lawsuit]] against OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT. A few of Apple's workers left the company and joined OpenAI, and Apple claims they {{walked off with}} [[confidential]] information to help {{come up with}} a new AI [[device]].

verbs.wrong: To become less successful than a rival
verbs.correct: To stop being partners after a quarrel

verbs.wrong: To leave a job suddenly, without warning
verbs.correct: To take something that does not belong to you

verbs.wrong: To improve a product that already exists
verbs.correct: To think of or create a new idea or plan

chunks.text: In its court papers, Apple {{lays out}} how it believes the [[theft]] happened. It says that before these workers left, they {{sent off}} private company files to their own personal email accounts. Apple now wants a [[judge]] to {{step in}} and stop OpenAI from using any of its [[trade secrets]].

verbs.wrong: To prove that something really happened
verbs.correct: To explain or describe something clearly

verbs.wrong: To hide something so that nobody can find it
verbs.correct: To send something to a place, often by email or mail

verbs.wrong: To make the final decision in a court case
verbs.correct: To get involved in order to help or stop a problem

chunks.text: OpenAI quickly {{hit back}} at the [[claims]]. A [[spokesperson]] for the company said that OpenAI has no interest in other companies' secrets, and that its lawyers are still {{going over}} the papers. So far, the two sides do not agree, and neither one will {{back down}}.

verbs.wrong: To refuse to answer questions about a problem
verbs.correct: To reply strongly to an attack or criticism

verbs.wrong: To correct the mistakes in a document
verbs.correct: To examine or check something carefully

verbs.wrong: To admit that you did something wrong
verbs.correct: To stop demanding something or stop arguing

chunks.text: The fight comes as Apple {{moves away}} from OpenAI in another way. Apple has announced that its voice [[assistant]], Siri, will soon {{run on}} Google's Gemini system instead of ChatGPT. Many people had expected the two companies to {{stick together}} for years to come, so the sudden change has surprised the whole tech world.

verbs.wrong: To be owned by another company
verbs.correct: To work using a certain kind of power

verbs.wrong: To share their technology with each other
verbs.correct: To stay united and continue to support each other

He fell out with his business partner over money.
Old friends sometimes fall out over small things.

vocab.def: To take something that does not belong to you
ex: Someone walked off with my phone at the gym.
A visitor walked off with two books from the library.
The thief walked off with her purse in seconds.

vocab.def: To think of or create a new idea or plan
ex: She came up with a great name for the show.
We need to come up with a plan by Friday.
He came up with a faster way to finish the job.

vocab.def: To explain or describe something clearly
ex: The teacher laid out the rules on the first day.
The report lays out the plan step by step.
She laid out her ideas at the meeting.

vocab.def: To send something to a place, often by email or mail
ex: I sent off the forms this morning.
He sent off an email before leaving work.
She sent off the package to her sister.

vocab.def: To get involved in order to help or stop a problem
ex: The teacher stepped in to stop the argument.
The government stepped in to save the bank.
A stranger stepped in and helped the lost child.

vocab.def: To reply strongly to an attack or criticism
ex: The actor hit back at the newspaper's story.
The company hit back at the report with facts.
She hit back at her critics in an interview.

vocab.def: To examine or check something carefully
ex: Go over your answers before the test ends.
The lawyer went over the contract twice.
We went over the plan one more time.

vocab.def: To stop demanding something or stop arguing
ex: Neither driver would back down after the accident.
He refused to back down in the debate.
The company finally backed down and changed the rule.
The firm is moving away from paper documents.
Many companies moved away from that old software.
She moved away from her early singing style.

vocab.def: To work using a certain kind of power
ex: This car runs on electricity.
The new phone runs on a faster system.
The whole factory runs on solar power.

vocab.def: To stay united and continue to support each other
ex: Our family sticks together in hard times.
The players stuck together after the loss.
Good friends stick together no matter what.

wordDefs.def: A legal case that one person or company brings against another in court
ex: The company faced a big lawsuit.
They started a lawsuit last year.

wordDefs.def: Meant to be kept secret and not shared with others
ex: The doctor keeps patient records confidential.
This report is confidential, so do not share it.

wordDefs.def: A machine or tool made for a certain job, like a phone
ex: This device can take photos.
A new device came out this month.
The theft happened at night.
Police are looking into the theft.

wordDefs.def: A person who leads a court and decides legal cases
ex: The judge listened to both sides.
A judge will decide the case.

wordDefs.def: Private business information that a company keeps hidden from others
ex: The recipe is a trade secret.
They protect their trade secrets carefully.

wordDefs.def: Statements that something is true, even without full proof yet
ex: He made big claims about the product.
The claims were hard to believe.

wordDefs.def: A person who speaks to the public for a company or group
ex: A spokesperson answered the questions.
The spokesperson read a short statement.

wordDefs.def: A person or program that helps you do things
ex: The voice assistant set an alarm.
My assistant booked the meeting.

tf.s: OpenAI has asked a judge to step in and stop Apple from selling the iPhone.
tf.why: False. It is Apple that wants a judge to step in and stop OpenAI from using its trade secrets.

tf.s: Both companies quickly agreed and ended the argument.
tf.why: The two sides do not agree, and neither one will back down.

tf.s: Apple has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI.
tf.why: The story says Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT.

tf.s: Apple's Siri will soon run on Google's Gemini instead of ChatGPT.
tf.why: Apple announced that Siri will run on Google's Gemini system instead of ChatGPT.

tf.s: OpenAI agreed that it had taken Apple's secrets.
tf.why: OpenAI hit back at the claims and said it has no interest in other companies' secrets.

tf.s: Apple says its former workers sent private files to their personal email accounts.
tf.why: Apple's court papers say the workers sent off private company files to their own personal email accounts before leaving.
